Hi Samantha — great to meet today. Quick recap from our call and a few ask items so we can reproduce and triage the 5xx you're seeing when calling the embeddings endpoint.

Summary from call:
- Finlytics is integrating Redwood embeddings for semantic search across their transactions index.
- Intermittent 5xx/502 responses on POST /v1/embeddings observed ~10% of calls during peak loads (mostly 10:30-11:30 PST).
- You're on a slightly customized request payload (50+ documents batched) and calling our hosted us-west1 region.

Immediate asks to help us reproduce:
1) Request-id / timestamp of a failing call (if available).
2) Full request payload (or a sanitized representative example).
3) SDK version and auth method (are you using API key in header or a short-lived token?).
4) Any gateway/proxy in front of Redwood that might be modifying payload sizes or timeouts.

What we'll do on our side:
- Vivek (cc'd) will give an immediate repro snippet and a quick checklist (timeout, SDK version, region routing).
- Dev Patel (support) will pick this up if we can get logs/request-ids and open SUP ticket for deeper trace.

Attachments: please attach the error logs if convenient (you mentioned there are a few). If you can paste a sanitized request body we can try to reproduce locally.

Proposed next step: If you can share the request-id from a failing call and the representative payload, we can be in a triage call tomorrow morning. Rishi and I will follow up on timeline for pilot once this is resolved.

Thanks —

Thanks Camila + Sam — quick triage checklist and a repro snippet that often isolates this class of failure.

Checklist (quick wins):
- Increase client timeout to 120s while we repro. Your 60s gateway timeout could cause cancellation and upstream 502 depending on how HTTP proxies respond.
- Confirm JS SDK version >= v1.3.2 (we fixed a streaming/batching bug in v1.3.2 that could cause malformed multipart payloads for larger batches).
- Try reducing batch size to 16-20 items to validate whether payload size contributes to the 5xx.
- Include X-Redwood-Request-Id header for easier tracing (we'll look for request-id in our logs).
- If you use a proxy/gateway, ensure it forwards the full body and doesn't apply additional chunking.

Repro curl (sanitized):
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings?region=us-west1" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Redwood-Request-Id: repro-embed-01" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-001","inputs":["doc1","doc2",...]}'

I've attached a small patch with a snippet that toggles the SDK batcher behavior (redwood_sdk_snippet.patch) — this is just to try locally and should not be used in prod without review.

If you can run the above with an increased timeout and give us the failing request-id (or repro-embed-01), we can trace. I'll take a look in logs once you share the request-id.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Sam — looping in to pick up the support work. I've opened SUP-1234 to track the deeper investigation.

Repro steps I ran locally against a sanitized copy of your payload (results attached in arch-diagram.png showing routing):
1) Run the curl provided by Vivek with region explicitly set to us-west1.
2) Set client timeout to 120s.
3) Run with batch sizes of 50 and 20 to compare.
4) Watch for backend response and record X-Request-Id from headers.

What I need from you to progress: 
- The request-id you pasted earlier (req_Gz9t4b2k) — can you confirm if that maps to the same time window in the attached logs?
- If possible, reproduce with X-Redwood-Request-Id header so we can find the exact invocation in our traces.

Preliminary findings from local repro: when batching at 50 we occasionally hit a gateway timeout between our edge and an internal upstream service; the stack shows 502 coming from an internal NLP worker (we're still instrumenting). Reducing batch size eliminated the failure in local runs.

I'll keep SUP-1234 updated and attach traces as we pull them.

--
